sentences.text: These video conferencing rules are dated 09.06.2020.
These rules are framed during the pandemic time.

If the petitioner is permitted to cross-examine from Canada through video conferencing as per Rule 5, there shall be a remote point co-ordinator at Canada and as per sub rule 5.3.1, it is the official of the Indian consulate/the relevant embassy/the relevant High Commission of India.

Considering the timeline between two countries, the officers of the Indian  - 10 -  NC: 2024:KHC:45654  WP No. 24228 of 2023 embassy has to be present during the night time, the petitioner has to be awake during the night time and work in the day time.

Further, it is a practical problem that for every case office of the Indian Embassy may not be able to depute its officers considering the number of people staying outside the country and number of divorce cases pending.
It is a practically impossible task.
Further, how many hours, or how many days it will take for the cross-examination depends up on the work load of the Court and other relevant factors.

That apart, in several cases the Hon'ble Apex Court in cases of appointing the advocate commissioner for recording of evidence has observed that in all cases, it is better to record the evidence before the Court as the Court will be able to look at the demeanor of the witness.
